correctness.rationale: Independently re-derived Rudin–Shapiro recursion r(2q)=r(q), r(2q+1)=r(q) xor (q mod2) and the eight-state maps T0,T1. Verified all states are reachable and the 4-step child transition matrix is positive, giving uniform state frequencies. Exhausted 8*16=128 state-residue cases for every n=1..16, reproducing exactly the 36 listed palindromes, their per-word multiplicities 64,32,16,4,8,4,2,2,2,1,1 and zero at lengths 9,11,13,15,16. Every longer palindrome contains central 15/16 palindrome, hence excluded. Pair density 1/128, so every listed density and position rule follow for infinitely many starts. A finite 32768-start sample was slightly nonuniform (n=1: 16512 versus 16256), as expected for a prefix and not contrary to the limiting density theorem.

evidence: Allouche et al. covers generalized Rudin-Shapiro palindrome complexity, not the submitted exact density table; prior cyclic-prefix theorem covers dyadic circular factors, not infinite word occurrence measures.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Scope broadens from factor existence/circular languages to occurrence densities for a specified classical word, not a routine corollary of those general statements.

evidence: A palindrome-length cutoff forbids long factors but does not determine frequency of any shorter one; universal automatic definability does not give the displayed equal densities without analysis.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge. The 2001 Allouche–Baake–Cassaigne–Damanik paper gives palindrome-length cutoff; Schaeffer–Shallit determine maximal palindromic words; the earlier cyclic-prefix published Resultary paper lists the same 36-word language. None of those inspected source statements provides all per-factor limiting starting-position densities or the eight-state exact starting-position rule, and mere knowledge of factor existence cannot imply the frequency of occurrence. Older inaccessible 1997 source remains a bounded priority risk.
residual_risks: 1997 historical Allouche paper available as abstract, not full original; unindexed per-factor frequency tables may predate the present.
Source-only eight-state calculation is exhaustive mathematically because of primitive recurrence, not because of a large finite prefix.
